quiz.title: Class 12 Integration Quiz
quiz.intro: Eight questions across the Class 12 integration toolkit — standard forms, substitution, by parts, partial fractions and definite integrals. Answer each, then press Check my score.

questions.explanation: Use the power rule ∫ x<sup>n</sup> dx = x<sup>n+1</sup>/(n+1) + C with n = 5, giving x<sup>6</sup>/6 + C.
The power rule fails at n = −1. This is the special standard form ∫ (1/x) dx = ln|x| + C.

questions.q: Using the substitution u = x<sup>2</sup>, what is ∫ 2x cos(x<sup>2</sup>) dx?
questions.explanation: With u = x<sup>2</sup>, du = 2x dx, so the integral becomes ∫ cos u du = sin u + C = sin(x<sup>2</sup>) + C.

questions.q: Integrate by parts: ∫ x e<sup>x</sup> dx = ?
questions.explanation: Take u = x, dv = e<sup>x</sup> dx. Then ∫ x e<sup>x</sup> dx = x e<sup>x</sup> − ∫ e<sup>x</sup> dx = x e<sup>x</sup> − e<sup>x</sup> + C = (x − 1) e<sup>x</sup> + C.

questions.q: In the partial-fraction split 1/[(x − 1)(x + 2)] = A/(x − 1) + B/(x + 2), what is A?
questions.explanation: Multiply through and set x = 1: 1 = A(1 + 2), so A = 1/3. (Setting x = −2 gives B = −1/3.)

questions.q: Evaluate the definite integral ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>1</sup> x<sup>2</sup> dx.
questions.explanation: The antiderivative is x<sup>3</sup>/3. Evaluating from 0 to 1 gives 1/3 − 0 = 1/3.

questions.q: Using the property for odd functions, what is ∫<sub>−2</sub><sup>2</sup> x<sup>3</sup> dx?
questions.explanation: x<sup>3</sup> is odd, and ∫<sub>−a</sub><sup>a</sup> f(x) dx = 0 when f is odd, so the integral is 0.
Since d/dx (tan x) = sec<sup>2</sup> x, the standard form gives ∫ sec<sup>2</sup> x dx = tan x + C.

faq.q: What topics does Class 12 integration cover?
faq.a: The CBSE Class 12 chapter covers integration as the reverse of differentiation, standard forms, integration by substitution, by parts, using partial fractions, definite integrals as limits of a sum, the fundamental theorem of calculus and the properties of definite integrals.

faq.q: When should I use integration by parts instead of substitution?
faq.a: Substitution works when part of the integrand is the derivative of another part, such as 2x cos(x squared). Integration by parts suits a product of two unlike functions, like x times e to the x, where the ILATE rule helps you choose which factor to differentiate.

faq.q: How do partial fractions help with integration?
faq.a: A proper rational function with a factorable denominator can be split into simpler fractions like A/(x minus 1) + B/(x + 2). Each piece integrates to a logarithm or a standard form, which is far easier than integrating the original fraction directly.

faq.q: Which properties of definite integrals are most useful in exams?
faq.a: The most used are that the integral of an odd function over a symmetric interval is zero, the even-function doubling rule, the king property that replaces x with a plus b minus x, and splitting the interval at a convenient point. These often turn a hard integral into a quick one.
